extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for (1) petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181) and (2) petitions to revive an abandoned application or accept late issue/publication/maintenance/payment under 37 CFR 1.137, including what replies, fees, statements, and supporting evidence are required and how timeliness/intentionality are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely petition to withdraw holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, any petition not filed within 2 months from the action complained of may be dismissed as untimely (37 CFR 1.181(f)). A petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment not filed within two months of the mail date of a notice of abandonment may be dismissed as untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than dismiss, the Office may require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition. Where the record indicates intentional delay, the Office may dismiss solely on that basis. See discussion of special rules by application type and filing date in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer required for untimely petitions — design/early utility/plant filings (received notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In design applications, utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, if applicant receives a notice of abandonment, any petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment not filed within two months of the mail date will not (absent extraordinary circumstances) be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and the required fee (37 CFR 1.20(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period to be disclaimed is the terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period between: (A) the date two months after the mail date of the notice of abandonment; and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment. See MPEP § 711.03(c) II.G for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer required for untimely petitions — design/early utility/plant filings (did not receive notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For those same application types, if the applicant never receives the notice of abandonment, any petition not filed within twelve months from the date of applicant’s filing (or submission, if correspondence was never received) of correspondence for which further action can reasonably be expected will not (absent extraordinary circumstances) be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period to be disclaimed is the terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period between: (A) the date twelve months from the applicant’s filing/submission of the correspondence for which further action can reasonably be expected; and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No terminal disclaimer ordinarily required — utility/plant filed June 8, 1995 to May 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, consult OPLA if the holding of abandonment involves periods during (A) appellate review by the PTAB, (B) an interference or derivation proceeding (35 U.S.C. 135) including any suspension due to such proceed., or (C) the application was sealed or prosecution suspended due to a secrecy order (35 U.S.C. 181), because patent term adjustment effects may need to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No terminal disclaimer ordinarily required — utility/plant filed on/after May 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is because patent term adjustment (PTA) is automatically reduced under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) or 1.704(a) for certain failures to file petitions within two months or when applicant does not receive notice; PTA reductions apply to post-AIPA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revival under 37 CFR 1.137 (types of failures covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 provides for revival of abandoned applications, or terminated/limited reexamination prosecution, on the basis of unintentional delay for failure: (A) to timely reply to an Office requirement in a provisional application; (B) to timely prosecute in a nonprovisional application; (C) to timely pay the issue fee for a design application; (D) to timely pay the issue fee for a utility or plant application; and (E) to provide copendency between the abandoned application and a subsequently filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories identify the factual bases that may support a 1.137 petition when the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition contents for 37 CFR 1.137 revival
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137 requires: (A) the required reply (unless previously filed); (B) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (C) any terminal disclaimer (and fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(d)) required pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137(d); and (D) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply from the due date until the filing of a grantable petition was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional; petitions filed more than two years after abandonment require extra explanation of circumstances surrounding the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement for 37 CFR 1.137 petitions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by the required reply, which generally is the reply sufficient to have avoided abandonment had it been timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136 and its fee are not required to be included with the reply. The required reply varies by the type of abandonment (see specific reply rules below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to submit specification/drawings under 37 CFR 1.57(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application abandoned under 37 CFR 1.57(a), the required reply must include a copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not required for revival, a certified copy of the previously filed application may be required for an application filed by reference; if required and not filed within the later of four months from filing date or sixteen months from earlier filing, a petition showing good and sufficient cause and the petition fee are required. See MPEP § 601.01(a) III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to pay issue fee or publication fee
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application abandoned for failure to timely pay the issue fee, the required reply must include the issue fee (and any required publication fee). The issue fee due with the petition is the dollar amount specified in the notice of allowance; if a publication fee was specified it must be paid in that dollar amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue fee is not an acceptable reply for applications abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee. An applicant may change entity status when filing the petition and pay the petition fee in the new status amount, but the issue/publication fees must be paid in the amounts specified on the notice of allowance. For timely issue fee payments (not revival), entity changes affect the required amount differently as explained in the Notice of Allowance guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to provide required drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application abandoned for failure to provide required drawings, a petition to revive will be dismissed unless the required drawings are filed before or with the petition to revive the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must be supplied as the required reply; no revival if drawings are not provided with the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to reply to a non-final action
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application abandoned for failure to reply to a non-final action, the required reply may be: (A) an argument or amendment under 37 CFR 1.111; or (B) the filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or a CPA under 1.53(d) for design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of a petition is not a determination that a 1.111 reply is complete; examiners may later find defects and issue a 2-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to correct errors. Extensions under 1.136(a) are permitted; failure to correct leads to re-abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to reply to a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final action must include: (A) a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee; (B) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 that cancels all rejected claims or otherwise prima facie places the application in condition for allowance; (C) filing of an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 (with submission meeting 1.111 and requisite fee) for certain post-June 8, 1995 applications; or (D) filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or CPA under 1.53(d) for design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is a proposed amendment under 1.116, the Office of Petitions will normally route the matter to the Technology Center to determine whether the amendment places the application in condition for allowance. Examiners should mark replies 'OK to enter upon revival' when appropriate; otherwise the Office of Petitions will not grant the petition and will use form PTOL-303 to advise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply — failure to file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Where abandonment occurred because an appeal brief was not filed, the reply required by 37 CFR 1.137(b)(1) must be either: (A) an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c); (B) filing an RCE accompanied by a compliant submission and fee (for certain post-June 8, 1995 applications); or (C) filing a continuing application (or CPA for design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Notice of Appeal is the reply, the time period under 37 CFR 41.37 for filing the appeal brief will be set by the Director in the decision granting the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an RCE as the required reply — responsiveness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE is filed as the reply under 37 CFR 1.137(b)(1), the submission accompanying the RCE must be a reply responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last Office action; responsiveness is judged without factoring in the 'final' status of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission may incorporate by reference arguments in a previously filed appeal or reply brief. The petition may be granted if the submission appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply; examiners may later find the reply lacking and will give a 2-month shortened statutory period under 1.135(c) for correction (extensions under 1.136(a) permitted). Failure to correct results in re-abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require continuing application or RCE where reply imposes inordinate burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require filing of a continuing application or an RCE (if prosecution prior to abandonment was closed) to meet the 1.137(b)(1) reply requirement where treating a reply under 1.111 or 1.113 would place an inordinate burden on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary circumstances include: (A) application abandoned for an inordinate period; (B) file contains multiple or conflicting replies to the last Office action; or (C) the reply(s) submitted are questionable as to compliance with 1.111 or 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication/foreign filing notice requirement and revival (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant made a nonpublication request and then files a counterpart application in a foreign country (or under an agreement requiring eighteen-month publication), the applicant must notify the USPTO within 45 days after such foreign filing; failure to timely provide that notice results in abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to timely notify the Office of a foreign filing may be revived only on the basis of unintentional delay under 37 CFR 1.137; the reply requirement of 1.137(c) is met by the notification, but filing a 1.137 petition will not stay any running reply period. Applicants may use forms PTO/SB/64a or PTO/SB/64/PTO/SB/64PCT and may file electronic ePetitions for certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee for revival and related petitions (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) requires that the Office charge $1,700 on filing each petition for revival of an abandoned application, for delayed payment of the issue fee, for delayed responses in reexamination, for delayed maintenance fee payments, for delayed submission of a priority/benefit claim, or for certain extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may refund part of the fee in 'exceptional circumstances' (e.g., widespread disaster) but not otherwise. The phrase 'on filing' means the fee is due on filing (not merely on grant); the Office will not reach merits of any petition lacking the requisite petition fee and generally will not refund the fee even if petition dismissed, absent exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay standard and evidentiary expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office usually relies on the applicant's duty of candor and accepts a statement that 'the entire delay...was unintentional' without further information in the vast majority of 1.137 petitions, but may require additional information where delay exceeds two years or other questions arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extended delay (>2 years from abandonment) raises doubt and requires additional explanation and supporting facts/correspondence. Deliberate decisions to permit abandonment (e.g., claims unpatentable, insufficient value, defer fees) are not 'unintentional' and cannot be cured by later change of mind or changed circumstances. Submitting an inappropriate/untruthful unintentionality statement can have serious consequences (e.g., inequitable conduct and unenforceability). See examples A–E of deliberate choices that preclude unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of delay — three periods to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating a 1.137 petition, consider three periods: (A) the delay in reply that originally resulted in abandonment; (B) the delay in filing an initial petition under 1.137 to revive; and (C) the delay in filing a grantable petition under 1.137 to revive the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intentional decision to abandon or to delay seeking revival cannot be considered unintentional, and such intentional delay is not cured by the correctness of prior office actions, discovery of new evidence, or later changes in circumstances.
